landmarks.name: 西丽佛祖庙
landmarks.snippet: West Li Buddha Ancestor Temple is a serene Buddhist temple in Shenzhen's Xili area, vital for local spiritual life. It honors Buddha with tranquil halls and draws devotees; historically, it traces to ancient worship sites revived in modern China for cultural preservation.

landmarks.name: Activate Regina
landmarks.snippet: Activate Regina is an entertainment attraction featuring interactive gaming experiences. It serves as a modern recreational hub for visitors and locals seeking active fun in Regina. The venue opened as part of the city's growing leisure offerings in the early 21st century.

landmarks.name: AFI Silver Theatre and Cultural Center
landmarks.snippet: AFI Silver Theatre and Cultural Center is a historic movie palace turned cultural hub in Silver Spring. It matters as a preserved Art Deco landmark hosting film festivals and education programs. The single most interesting fact is its original 1938 opening featured the first air-conditioned theater in Maryland.

landmarks.name: All Saints Roman Catholic Church
landmarks.snippet: A prominent Roman Catholic parish church with deep community roots. It matters for its longstanding role in local worship and social services. The most interesting fact is its dedication to multiple saints, reflecting diverse immigrant influences.

landmarks.name: All Saints, West Ham
landmarks.snippet: All Saints, West Ham is a historic Anglican church in Stratford, London. Dating to the 12th century, it is the area's oldest surviving building and a key landmark. The church features medieval architecture and memorials to local figures.

landmarks.name: Amfiteáter
landmarks.snippet: The open-air theatre hosts major summer festivals. Built in the 1960s it became the cultural heart of the Tatra foothills.

landmarks.name: Anniversary Park Cenotaph
landmarks.snippet: A solemn war memorial honoring local veterans. It matters as the town’s central site of remembrance. The most interesting fact is that its plaques list Chestermere residents who served in both World Wars.

landmarks.name: Annunciation Orthodox Cathedral
landmarks.snippet: Annunciation Orthodox Cathedral is the main Eastern Orthodox cathedral serving Ottawa's Orthodox community. It matters as a spiritual and cultural hub for Greek and other Orthodox faithful. Built in 1997, it features traditional Byzantine domes and icons.

landmarks.name: Arco de la Maestranza y Parque de Artillería de Daoiz y Velarde
landmarks.snippet: A monumental arch erected in 1881 honoring artillery officers Daoiz and Velarde, heroes of the 1808 Dos de Mayo uprising against Napoleon.

landmarks.name: Art in the Park
landmarks.snippet: Art in the Park is a public sculpture installation in Princes Risborough. It matters as a modern community art project enhancing local green space. The most interesting fact is that it was created through collaboration between local artists and residents.

landmarks.name: Bürkliplatz
landmarks.snippet: Bürkliplatz is a central square and viewpoint at Lake Zurich's edge, serving as a hub for markets and events. It matters as a popular gathering spot. The most interesting fact is its location at the Quaibrücke offering panoramic lake and Alps views.

landmarks.name: Ballastbrygga industrihistoriske senter
landmarks.snippet: Ballastbrygga is an industrial history center in Mandal focusing on maritime trade and shipbuilding. It matters for preserving the port's economic legacy. The single most interesting fact is its original 19th-century ballast pier still visible in the exhibits.

landmarks.name: Bantayog ng mga Bayani Museum
landmarks.snippet: Located within the Bantayog complex, the museum preserves documents, photographs, and personal artifacts from the Marcos-era resistance, offering a powerful narrative of courage and sacrifice. It houses the original People Power Commission archives.

landmarks.name: Bantayog ng mga Bayani
landmarks.snippet: A monument and museum honoring martyrs and heroes of the fight against dictatorship in the Philippines, it stands as the nation’s primary site of remembrance for those who resisted authoritarian rule. The complex’s central obelisk is etched with the names of over 150 victims.

landmarks.name: Barrowfields
landmarks.snippet: Barrowfields is an Iron Age burial ground overlooking Newquay Bay. It matters as evidence of early settlement in Cornwall. The site contains prehistoric barrows that reveal ancient burial practices.

landmarks.name: Basílica de Nuestra Señora de Atocha
landmarks.snippet: A 20th-century basilica built over a 16th-century shrine. It houses the tombs of Spain’s royal family and commemorates the 2004 Madrid train bombings.

landmarks.name: Bath Abbey
landmarks.snippet: Bath Abbey is a late-medieval Gothic church and former cathedral rebuilt in the 16th century. It matters as the coronation site of King Edgar in 973, founding the idea of a united England. Its most striking detail: 52 windows create the nickname 'Lantern of the West'.

landmarks.name: Bath World Heritage Centre
landmarks.snippet: Interpretive museum explaining how Bath earned UNESCO status. Highlights include a detailed model of the Roman city and rare watercolours by Thomas Gainsborough.

landmarks.name: Battistero di San Giovanni in Fonte
landmarks.snippet: The Battistero di San Giovanni in Fonte is Verona's 12th-century octagonal baptistery next to the cathedral. It matters as a rare surviving Romanesque baptismal site. Its most interesting fact is the large pink Verona marble font carved from a single Roman sarcophagus block.

landmarks.name: Battle of Fort Dearborn
landmarks.snippet: Marks the 1812 massacre site that ended the first Fort Dearborn. The event shaped early Chicago and is commemorated here as the city's founding conflict.

landmarks.name: Bazilika svatého Jiří
landmarks.snippet: Bazilika svatého Jiří is the oldest surviving church building in Prague Castle, founded around 920. It matters as a key Romanesque landmark and royal burial site. The most interesting fact is it contains the tombs of early Přemyslid dukes including Saint Wenceslaus's grandmother.

landmarks.name: Bethesda United Presbyterian
landmarks.snippet: A historic Presbyterian congregation in Elizabeth, founded in the 19th century. Its architecture reflects Victorian Gothic style, and it served as an important spiritual and social center for the city's growing immigrant communities.

landmarks.name: BFI IMAX
landmarks.snippet: BFI IMAX is Europe's largest cinema screen, opened in 1999 under Waterloo Bridge. It screens documentaries and blockbusters in 3D. It replaced a 1951 Festival of Britain structure on the same site.

landmarks.name: Biblioteca del Dipartimento universitario clinico di biomedicina
landmarks.snippet: A specialized university library in Trieste focused on biomedical sciences. It matters for supporting medical research and education. The most interesting fact is that it contains rare 19th-century medical texts donated by Trieste's Jewish physicians.

landmarks.name: Biblioteca Mário de Andrade
landmarks.snippet: São Paulo's main public library founded in 1925, housing over 3.2 million items. Its 1929 Art Deco building features Brazil's first public children's library.

landmarks.name: Bibliothèque Polonaise de Paris
landmarks.snippet: Bibliothèque Polonaise de Paris is the oldest Polish library outside Poland. It matters for preserving Polish literature and history. Its most interesting fact is it was founded in 1838 by Polish exiles after the November Uprising.

landmarks.name: Bibliothek und Archiv des Instituts für Zeitgeschichte München-Berlin
landmarks.snippet: This library and archive preserves documents on 20th-century German history. It matters for research into the Nazi era and post-war developments. The single most interesting fact is its role in housing original records from the Nuremberg trials era.

landmarks.name: Boambee Lookout
landmarks.snippet: Boambee Lookout provides sweeping views over the coastline. It matters as a popular picnic and photography spot. The most interesting fact is hang-gliders launch from its cliffs on windy days.

landmarks.name: Boston Children's Museum
landmarks.snippet: The second-oldest children's museum in the US, opened in 1913. It matters for pioneering interactive learning for kids. The most interesting fact is it once housed a real Japanese house reassembled from Kyoto.

landmarks.name: Boston Fire Museum
landmarks.snippet: A historic firehouse museum preserving Boston's firefighting heritage. It matters as home to antique engines and equipment from the city's past. The most interesting fact is it occupies an 1891 fire station that survived the Great Boston Fire.

landmarks.name: Boston Tea Party - Ships and Museum
landmarks.snippet: A floating museum featuring replicas of the 1773 tea ships. It matters as the site of the protest that sparked the American Revolution. The most interesting fact is that visitors can still throw replica tea chests overboard today.

landmarks.name: Broadway United Church
landmarks.snippet: Broadway United Church is a historic place of worship in Regina emphasizing community service and faith. It matters for its longstanding role in local religious life. Founded in the early 20th century, it has hosted significant community gatherings reflecting Regina's social history.

landmarks.name: Brown Theatre
landmarks.snippet: Brown Theatre is a landmark 1925 performing arts venue in Louisville's theatre district, known for its Renaissance Revival style and role in hosting Broadway tours. It matters for cultural contributions; it was renovated in 2017 after decades of service.

landmarks.name: Bruen Chapel Methodist Church
landmarks.snippet: Historic Methodist church in Falls Church, VA, dating to the early 19th century. One of Fairfax County's oldest congregations. Fact: Established around 1825, it served as a Union hospital during the Civil War and retains its original stone structure.

landmarks.name: Callery Gorge Bridge
landmarks.snippet: Callery Gorge Bridge is a scenic suspension footbridge near Franz Josef offering dramatic gorge views. It matters for providing safe access to otherwise inaccessible natural beauty. The bridge replaced an earlier structure destroyed by floods in 1965.

landmarks.name: Captain Arthur Phillip R.N.
landmarks.snippet: Captain Arthur Phillip R.N. is a memorial honoring the first Governor of New South Wales. It matters as a tribute to the founder of the Australian colony. The most interesting fact is it commemorates his 1788 landing near Manly, initiating British settlement.

landmarks.name: Casa de Dona Yayá
landmarks.snippet: Historic 1890s mansion turned cultural center, once home to an heiress who lived as a recluse. Preserves original Art Nouveau interiors and the city's oldest elevator.

landmarks.name: Casa do Alentejo
landmarks.snippet: It is a cultural center in a historic palace promoting Alentejo traditions. The building features stunning azulejo tiles and Moorish architectural elements.

landmarks.name: Casa Memoria José Domingo Cañas
landmarks.snippet: This memorial house commemorates victims of Chile's military dictatorship held and tortured at 1367 José Domingo Cañas street. It stands as a site of memory and human rights education. Its most powerful detail is the preserved torture chamber now open to visitors.

landmarks.name: Casa Museo Eduardo Frei Montalva
landmarks.snippet: This museum preserves the home of Eduardo Frei Montalva, Chile's president from 1964 to 1970. It highlights his reformist legacy and centrist politics. The most striking fact is that Frei remains Chile's only leader to serve two non-consecutive terms.

landmarks.name: Castello di Dosso
landmarks.snippet: A medieval castle overlooking Lake Maggiore. It matters as a key defensive stronghold controlling Alpine trade routes. The most interesting fact is that its keep still bears 14th-century frescoes depicting the castle’s own construction.

landmarks.name: Cathedral of the Assumption
landmarks.snippet: The Cathedral of the Assumption is Louisville's oldest cathedral and a stunning example of Neo-Gothic architecture, serving as the seat of the Archdiocese since 1852. It matters for its role in local Catholic history; interestingly, it hosted Abraham Lincoln's funeral procession in 1865.

landmarks.name: Cattedrale di Santa Maria Matricolare
landmarks.snippet: The Cathedral of Santa Maria Matricolare is Verona's main cathedral and a key Romanesque landmark. It matters as the seat of the local bishopric since the 5th century. Its most interesting fact is the 12th-century marble porch by Maestro Nicolò featuring Jonah and the whale carvings.

landmarks.name: Central Library
landmarks.snippet: Central Library is Huntington Beach's main public library. It matters as the city's central hub for knowledge and community programs. The most interesting fact is it houses extensive local history archives dating back to the city's founding in 1909.

landmarks.name: 中環至半山自動扶手電梯系統 Central-Mid-Levels Escalator System
landmarks.snippet: The Central-Mid-Levels Escalator is the world's longest outdoor covered escalator system. It matters as a daily transport link for residents and tourists. The most interesting fact is it reverses direction in the afternoon to serve downhill commuters.

landmarks.name: Central Wandandian Public School 1911
landmarks.snippet: Central Wandandian Public School 1911 is a heritage-listed one-room schoolhouse now operating as a small museum. It preserves original desks and a 1912 roll book listing 14 pupils from pioneer families.

landmarks.name: Chestermere Public Library
landmarks.snippet: The town’s main public library serving thousands of residents. It matters as the cultural and educational hub of Chestermere. The most interesting fact is its annual ‘Frozen Lake Reads’ winter reading challenge held on the ice.

landmarks.name: Chestermere Sailboat
landmarks.snippet: A public sculpture celebrating the lake’s sailing culture. It matters as a beloved photo spot and local landmark. The most interesting fact is that the stainless-steel sail was donated by the Chestermere Yacht Club in 2005.

landmarks.name: Chiesa cristiana degli Avventisi del Settimo Giorno Movimento di Riforma
landmarks.snippet: A Seventh-day Adventist Reform Movement church in Trieste. It matters as a minority Protestant congregation in a predominantly Catholic city. The most interesting fact is that it was established by Eastern European refugees in the 1920s.

landmarks.name: Chiesa dei Santi Ippolito e Cassiano
landmarks.snippet: A hillside church dedicated to the twin soldier-martyrs. It matters for preserving Romanesque architecture amid Ticino’s Baroque churches. The most interesting fact is that a crypt beneath the nave still contains fragments of a 5th-century baptistery mosaic.

landmarks.name: Chiesa della Beata Vergine delle Grazie
landmarks.snippet: A historic Roman Catholic church in Trieste. It matters for its Baroque architecture and role as a pilgrimage site. The most interesting fact is that it houses a 17th-century miraculous fresco of the Virgin Mary believed to have healed many devotees.

landmarks.name: Chiesa di San Rocco
landmarks.snippet: A small lakeside church dedicated to the plague saint. It matters for its role in the community’s annual rogation processions. The most interesting fact is that its simple façade hides a fresco cycle from 1519 showing local villagers in period dress.

landmarks.name: Chiesa parrocchiale Santa Teresa del Bambino Gesù
landmarks.snippet: A modern parish church in Trieste dedicated to St. Thérèse of Lisieux. It matters for serving the local Catholic community. The most interesting fact is that its construction was funded by donations from Trieste's Catholic faithful after World War II.

landmarks.name: Children with Kites
landmarks.snippet: Children with Kites is a beloved public artwork by artist Michael Bast, depicting joyful children flying kites, installed in Louisville. It matters as a symbol of childhood wonder in urban spaces; it's part of the city's vibrant public art collection.

landmarks.name: Chrám sv. Petra a Pavla
landmarks.snippet: This 13th-century Gothic church anchors Poprad's historic center. It features rare medieval frescoes that survived multiple renovations over centuries.

landmarks.name: Christ Church Cathedral
landmarks.snippet: Christ Church Cathedral is the oldest church building in continuous use in Louisville, built in 1824 as the mother church of the Episcopal Diocese of Kentucky. It matters for its historical significance; it survived the 1937 Ohio River flood largely intact.

landmarks.name: Christ Church Cathedral
landmarks.snippet: Christ Church Cathedral is Ottawa's Anglican cathedral and seat of the Bishop of Ottawa. It matters as a central place of worship and community gathering. Its Gothic Revival architecture was consecrated in 1873 after the original wooden structure burned down.

landmarks.name: Christ Church, Leyton
landmarks.snippet: Christ Church is a Victorian Anglican parish church built in 1854. It matters as one of Leyton’s earliest major religious buildings serving a rapidly growing suburb. Most interesting fact: its spire was once the tallest structure in the district and used as a navigational landmark.

landmarks.name: Christuskirche
landmarks.snippet: Christuskirche is a Protestant church in Munich known for its community gatherings and services. It matters as a historic site of worship and local identity. The single most interesting fact is that it survived World War II damage and was rebuilt as a symbol of peace.

landmarks.name: Church of Saint Mary the Virgin
landmarks.snippet: The Church of Saint Mary the Virgin is an Anglo-Catholic parish known as Smoky Mary's for its heavy use of incense. Founded in 1868, its current French Gothic building opened in 1895 and features one of the city's largest pipe organs.

landmarks.name: Church of St Stephen
landmarks.snippet: Church of St Stephen is an Anglican parish church serving the local community. It matters for its role in Singapore's Christian heritage and outreach programs. The most interesting fact is its founding in 1963 as one of the early modern churches in the area.

landmarks.name: Coastguard's Lookout
landmarks.snippet: Coastguard's Lookout is a historic watchpoint on Towan Head. It matters for its role in maritime safety and rescue. From here coastguards monitored shipping and coordinated lifeboat launches.

landmarks.name: Coliseu dos Recreios
landmarks.snippet: It is a historic multi-purpose venue for concerts, opera and circus since 1890. It hosted legendary performances by Amália Rodrigues and international stars.

landmarks.name: Commemoration
landmarks.snippet: A modern public artwork celebrating the town’s heritage. The sculpture marks the former site of the old railway station, linking past and present.

landmarks.name: Congregation Olam Tikvah Synogogue
landmarks.snippet: A Reform Jewish synagogue in Fairfax, VA, serving the community since 1975. It matters as a center for Jewish life and learning in Northern Virginia. Interesting fact: Named 'Olam Tikvah' meaning 'hope for the world,' it hosts vibrant cultural events and interfaith dialogues.

landmarks.name: Crabbe Library
landmarks.snippet: The main library at Eastern Kentucky University serving students and researchers. It matters for preserving regional history and academic resources. The most interesting fact is it houses extensive Appalachian and Kentucky history collections including rare manuscripts.

landmarks.name: Custom House Tower Observation Deck
landmarks.snippet: The Custom House Tower Observation Deck offers panoramic views from Boston's first skyscraper, completed in 1915. The 496-foot tower was the tallest in New England for 49 years.

landmarks.name: Daniel Boone Statue
landmarks.snippet: A prominent public artwork honoring frontiersman Daniel Boone. It matters as a tribute to Kentucky's pioneer heritage in Richmond. The most interesting fact is that Boone himself explored and hunted in the surrounding Bluegrass region during his expeditions.

landmarks.name: Duffy Square
landmarks.snippet: Duffy Square is the northern half of Times Square and home to the TKTS discount ticket booth. It honors Father Francis P. Duffy, a World War I hero and the most decorated U.S. chaplain in history.

landmarks.name: Edgewater Historical Society
landmarks.snippet: Edgewater Historical Society is a local history museum in Chicago. It matters for documenting the neighborhood's development. The most interesting fact is that it operates from a historic firehouse built in 1884.

landmarks.name: Edifício Copan
landmarks.snippet: Iconic modernist residential complex designed by Oscar Niemeyer in 1966, symbol of São Paulo's urban growth. The wave-like concrete facade makes it one of Brazil's most photographed buildings.

landmarks.name: Edward Ricketts Memorial
landmarks.snippet: Memorial to marine biologist Edward Ricketts, Steinbeck's friend. It honors his pioneering work on intertidal ecology along Cannery Row.

landmarks.name: EKU Center for the Arts
landmarks.snippet: A modern performing arts venue on Eastern Kentucky University's campus. It matters as the region's premier theater hosting concerts, plays, and lectures. The most interesting fact is it opened in 2011 and quickly became a cultural hub drawing national performers.

landmarks.name: Elizabeth Baptist Church
landmarks.snippet: A longstanding Baptist congregation in Elizabeth, founded in the late 1800s. It became a vital institution for African American worship and civil rights advocacy throughout the 20th century, reflecting the city's evolving cultural landscape.

landmarks.name: Elizabeth United Methodist Church
landmarks.snippet: Established in 1849, this United Methodist church is one of Elizabeth's oldest continuously active congregations. It became a center for abolitionist activity in the 19th century, sheltering freedom seekers on the Underground Railroad.

landmarks.name: Epiphany of Our Lord Byzantine Catholic Church
landmarks.snippet: A Byzantine Catholic church in Annandale, VA, known for its Eastern Rite liturgy and stunning iconography. It preserves Ukrainian heritage in America. Fact: Built in 1989, its architecture blends Byzantine and Ukrainian styles with a golden onion dome.

landmarks.name: Faneuil Hall Marketplace
landmarks.snippet: Faneuil Hall Marketplace is a historic market complex and meeting hall central to Boston's commerce and civic life since 1742. It hosted debates by Samuel Adams that fueled the American Revolution.

landmarks.name: Farmācijas muzejs
landmarks.snippet: The Pharmacy Museum displays the history of medicine and pharmaceuticals in Latvia. It matters as the oldest pharmacy in the Baltic states, operating since 1709. Most interesting fact: visitors can see original 18th-century apothecary equipment and herbal remedies.

landmarks.name: First Baptist Church
landmarks.snippet: A historic church congregation in Richmond with deep community roots. It matters as one of the area's longstanding places of worship. The most interesting fact is its continuous operation since the 19th century reflecting local religious heritage.

landmarks.name: First Presbyterian Church of Elizabeth
landmarks.snippet: Historic Presbyterian church in Elizabeth, NJ, founded in 1664 as the oldest Protestant church in the state. It played a key role during the American Revolution, hosting Continental Army soldiers and serving as a community hub for over 350 years.

landmarks.name: First Unitarian Universalist Church of San Diego
landmarks.snippet: First Unitarian Universalist Church of San Diego is a historic place of worship known for progressive values. It matters for its role in social justice movements. The single most interesting historical fact is that the congregation has advocated for civil rights since the 1950s.

landmarks.name: First United Methodist Church
landmarks.snippet: Founded in 1787, this is one of the earliest Methodist congregations in New Jersey. It survived multiple rebuilds after fires and remains a testament to Elizabeth's religious diversity and resilience through centuries of change.

landmarks.name: Forte da Bandeira
landmarks.snippet: 17th-century coastal fortress guarding the harbor. Matters as a key defensive landmark. Most interesting fact: served as a quarantine station during 19th-century cholera outbreaks.

landmarks.name: Franz Josef
landmarks.snippet: Franz Josef is a renowned glacier viewpoint in New Zealand's Westland Tai Poutini National Park, drawing visitors worldwide. It matters for showcasing dramatic ice formations shaped by millennia. The glacier was named after Emperor Franz Joseph I of Austria by explorer Julius von Haast in 1865.

landmarks.name: Fraumünster Kreuzgang
landmarks.snippet: Fraumünster Kreuzgang is the medieval cloister attached to the Fraumünster church. It matters for preserving 12th-14th century frescoes and architecture. The single most interesting fact is its well-preserved Romanesque and Gothic wall paintings depicting biblical scenes.

landmarks.name: Fraumünster
landmarks.snippet: Fraumünster is a historic church in Zurich founded in 853 as a Benedictine abbey for noblewomen. It matters for its role in medieval religious and civic life. The single most interesting fact is its five stained-glass windows designed by Marc Chagall in 1970.

landmarks.name: Galleria d'arte San Giusto
landmarks.snippet: A contemporary art gallery in Trieste dedicated to local and regional artists. It matters for preserving and showcasing the area's artistic heritage. The most interesting fact is that it was founded in a former 19th-century synagogue building.

landmarks.name: Gil Eannes
landmarks.snippet: Memorial ship honoring explorer Gil Eannes. Matters for its role in Portuguese maritime history. Most interesting fact: the vessel itself is a restored hospital ship from 1955.

landmarks.name: Glen Elm Branch
landmarks.snippet: Glen Elm Branch is a public library serving the Regina community with books, resources, and programs. It matters as a cornerstone of local education and literacy. Established to support neighborhood learning, it reflects Regina's commitment to accessible public knowledge.

landmarks.name: Gleniffer Braes
landmarks.snippet: Gleniffer Brae is a scenic viewpoint overlooking Paisley. It matters as a popular local park offering panoramic views of the city and countryside. The most interesting fact is its role as the setting for Robert Tannahill's poetry, linking it to Scotland's cultural heritage.

landmarks.name: Glessner House Museum
landmarks.snippet: Completed in 1887, this is Chicago's finest surviving example of the work of architect H.H. Richardson. It preserves original interiors and tells the story of Gilded Age Chicago.

landmarks.name: Église Saint-Louis-en-l'Île
landmarks.snippet: Église Saint-Louis-en-l'Île is a 17th-century Baroque church on Île Saint-Louis. It matters as a historic place of worship and community hub. Its most interesting fact is its organ, originally from the Saint-Germain-des-Prés abbey, installed in 1745.

landmarks.name: Gondola Rides at the Venetian
landmarks.snippet: Indoor and outdoor gondola rides through the Venetian Resort's Grand Canal. Introduced in 1999, they recreate Venice's waterways under a painted sky. The gondoliers sing traditional Italian songs while steering, making it one of the Strip's most romantic attractions.

landmarks.name: Governor's Mansion
landmarks.snippet: Utah's official governor residence since 1902. The Beaux-Arts mansion was built by silver magnate Thomas Kearns and became the state's executive home in 1937, offering a glimpse into Gilded Age wealth and politics.

landmarks.name: Gurudwara Singh Sabha
landmarks.snippet: Gurudwara Singh Sabha is Madrid's main Sikh temple offering worship and community services. It matters as a cultural bridge for the Sikh diaspora in Spain. The most interesting fact is it hosts the largest annual Vaisakhi festival celebrations in the city.

landmarks.name: Hammond Public Library
landmarks.snippet: A historic public library serving as a central educational and cultural hub. It matters for preserving local history and providing community resources. The most interesting fact is its role in early 20th-century literacy programs that shaped generations of residents.

landmarks.name: Helmhaus
landmarks.snippet: Helmhaus is a historic building now hosting contemporary art exhibitions in Zurich. It matters as a cultural venue since the 18th century. The single most interesting fact is its location on the site of a medieval water mill by the Limmat river.

landmarks.name: Henry B. Clarke House
landmarks.snippet: Oldest house in Chicago, built in 1836. It is the city's only surviving structure from its founding era and now serves as a museum of early Chicago domestic life.

landmarks.name: High Roller
landmarks.snippet: At 550 feet tall, the High Roller is the world's tallest observation wheel. Located at The LINQ, it offers 30-minute rides with sweeping views of the Strip and surrounding desert. Completed in 2014, it replaced the Stratosphere SkyJump as the highest point in Las Vegas.

landmarks.name: Historic Hillcrest Sign
landmarks.snippet: Historic Hillcrest Sign is a landmark monument in San Diego marking the entrance to the Hillcrest neighborhood. It matters as a symbol of community identity and local pride. The single most interesting historical fact is that it was originally erected in 1940 and restored in 1989.

landmarks.name: Historic Takoma
landmarks.snippet: Historic Takoma is a local history library and archive preserving Takoma Park's heritage. It matters as the community's key resource for documenting Victorian-era development. The single most interesting fact is it holds original 1880s land deeds from the town's founding.

landmarks.name: Hobbit
landmarks.snippet: Hobbit is an outdoor artwork installation inspired by Tolkien's world, located in the Franz Josef region. It matters as a unique cultural landmark blending fantasy with local artistry. The sculpture was created by a local artist using native timber and stone.

landmarks.name: Holy Family Catholic Church
landmarks.snippet: Holy Family Catholic Church is a place of worship. It matters as a historic Catholic parish in the area. The most interesting fact is its dedication to family values central to Catholic tradition.

landmarks.name: 香港海事博物館 Hong Kong Maritime Museum
landmarks.snippet: The Hong Kong Maritime Museum explores the city's seafaring history. It matters for preserving artifacts from the Opium Wars and trade routes. The most interesting fact is it is housed in a historic 19th-century pier building at Central.

landmarks.name: Hood Milk Bottle
landmarks.snippet: A 40-foot-tall wooden milk bottle built in 1930. It matters as an iconic piece of American roadside architecture. Most interesting fact: originally an ice cream stand, it now stands outside the Children's Museum.

landmarks.name: Huer's Hut
landmarks.snippet: Huer's Hut is a historic stone lookout tower on Newquay's headland. It matters as a rare survivor of Cornwall's pilchard fishing industry. Fishermen once used it to spot shoals and direct boats with a giant horn.

landmarks.name: Iglesia de las Agustinas
landmarks.snippet: Iglesia de las Agustinas is a historic Catholic church in Santiago built in neoclassical style. It serves as an important religious and architectural landmark. The most interesting fact is its original 17th-century founding by Augustinian nuns who helped shape early colonial Santiago.

landmarks.name: Iglesia ni Cristo
landmarks.snippet: Iglesia ni Cristo is a distinctive church building serving the Filipino Christian community. It represents the growth of global Christian denominations in London. The architecture stands out in the local streetscape.

landmarks.name: Igreja de São Luís dos Franceses
landmarks.snippet: It is an 17th-century church serving the French community in Lisbon. It features ornate baroque interiors and houses significant religious art.

landmarks.name: Igreja de São Sebastião
landmarks.snippet: Igreja de São Sebastião is a historic Baroque church dedicated to the town’s patron saint. It matters for its ornate interior and role in local religious festivals. The single most interesting fact is that its gilded altarpiece survived the 1755 earthquake largely intact.

landmarks.name: Igreja de Santo António
landmarks.snippet: Baroque church central to local worship. Matters for its ornate gilded interior. Most interesting fact: one of few churches spared major earthquake damage in 1755.

landmarks.name: Igreja Matriz
landmarks.snippet: Igreja Matriz is the main parish church of Albufeira, serving as the historic religious center of the town since medieval times. It matters for its central role in community life and architecture. The single most interesting fact is that its bell tower was once used as a defensive lookout during pirate raids.

landmarks.name: Inang Bayan Monument
landmarks.snippet: This memorial sculpture personifies the Philippines as a grieving mother, commemorating national loss and resilience. Positioned near key government buildings, it has become a focal point for civic ceremonies and public reflection.

landmarks.name: Institut du Monde arabe
landmarks.snippet: The Institut du Monde arabe is a museum and cultural center dedicated to Arab art, history, and science. It matters as a bridge between Arab and French cultures. Its most interesting fact is its south facade with 240 motor-controlled apertures that automatically adjust like a camera lens.

landmarks.name: Isaac Albéniz
landmarks.snippet: Isaac Albéniz is a memorial dedicated to the renowned Spanish composer in Madrid. It matters for celebrating his contributions to classical music. The most interesting fact is he composed his famous suite Iberia while traveling across Spain and Europe.

landmarks.name: Jin Long Si Temple
landmarks.snippet: Jin Long Si Temple is a historic Chinese temple in Singapore. It matters as a longstanding site of Taoist worship and community rituals. The most interesting fact is its rare dragon deity enshrined, believed to bring prosperity.

landmarks.name: John F. Kennedy Branch Gary Public Library
landmarks.snippet: A branch of the Gary Public Library system serving the Glen Park community. It matters as a vital educational and cultural hub in an underserved area. The single most interesting fact is its naming after President John F. Kennedy shortly after his 1963 assassination.

landmarks.name: John Steinbeck Memorial
landmarks.snippet: Memorial honoring John Steinbeck, Nobel-winning author of Cannery Row. It marks Monterey's literary legacy and his deep ties to the area's fishing history.

landmarks.name: Julius Caesar Statue at Caesars Palace Las Vegas
landmarks.snippet: A 14-foot bronze statue of Julius Caesar stands at the entrance of Caesars Palace. Installed in 1966, it symbolizes the resort's Roman theme. The statue has become an iconic photo spot and marks the first major themed architecture on the Strip.

landmarks.name: Kastellet
landmarks.snippet: Kastellet is a historic viewpoint overlooking Mandal's harbor and coastline. It matters as a former defensive site with panoramic views. The single most interesting fact is its use during the Napoleonic Wars for signaling ships entering the fjord.

landmarks.name: Katedrála svatého Víta, Václava a Vojtěcha
landmarks.snippet: Katedrála svatého Víta, Václava a Vojtěcha is Prague's Gothic cathedral and spiritual heart of the Czech lands. It matters as the coronation site of Bohemian kings. The most interesting fact is its construction spanned over 600 years from 1344 to 1929.

landmarks.name: Konkatedrála Sedembolestnej Panny Márie
landmarks.snippet: It is the main Catholic cathedral in Poprad serving as a key religious and cultural hub. Its striking neo-Gothic architecture from 1932 draws visitors from across the region.

landmarks.name: Kostol sv. Cyrila a Metoda
landmarks.snippet: Modern church honoring the Slavic apostles Cyril and Methodius, symbolizing national heritage. Its construction in the 20th century marks the town's post-war spiritual revival.

landmarks.name: Kostol sv. Egídia
landmarks.snippet: A historic church marking Poprad's medieval origins. It contains a 14th-century bell tower still used for community events today.

landmarks.name: Krišjāņa Barona muzejs
landmarks.snippet: Museum dedicated to the collector of Latvian folk songs. It preserves thousands of dainas and showcases 19th-century cultural heritage.

landmarks.name: Lady Denman Heritage Complex
landmarks.snippet: The Lady Denman Heritage Complex is a major cultural attraction preserving the region’s maritime history. It houses the restored ferry Lady Denman, built in 1911, which once carried passengers across Sydney Harbour.

landmarks.name: Las Vegas Strip
landmarks.snippet: A 4.2-mile stretch of Las Vegas Boulevard famous for its concentration of resort hotels and casinos. It is the most visited place in Nevada and the source of most of the city's tourism revenue. The Strip's neon lights were first installed in the 1940s, establishing Las Vegas as the entertainment capital of the world.

landmarks.name: Latvijas Nacionālā opera un balets
landmarks.snippet: The Latvian National Opera and Ballet is Riga's premier performing arts venue, hosting world-class opera and ballet since 1922. It matters as Latvia's cultural flagship. Most interesting fact: Richard Wagner conducted here in 1837-1838, influencing his later compositions.

landmarks.name: Latvijas Nacionālais dabas muzejs
landmarks.snippet: The Latvian National Museum of Natural History showcases Latvia's biodiversity and geological heritage. It matters as the country's oldest natural history museum, founded in 1846. Most interesting fact: it houses over 200,000 specimens including rare Baltic amber inclusions.

landmarks.name: Laurie Cunningham
landmarks.snippet: Laurie Cunningham memorial commemorates the trailblazing footballer who played for Leyton Orient before starring at Real Madrid. It matters as a tribute to a local hero who broke barriers as one of England’s first Black internationals. Most interesting fact: he scored the winning goal in the 1981 European Cup Winners’ Cup final.

landmarks.name: LDS Tenth Ward Square
landmarks.snippet: Historic Mormon meetinghouse complex dating to 1880. The square preserves Salt Lake City's pioneer-era grid plan and remains an active hub for neighborhood worship and community events.

landmarks.name: Legacy International
landmarks.snippet: Legacy International is a museum in San Diego dedicated to cultural and historical exhibits. It matters for preserving and showcasing diverse legacies. The single most interesting historical fact is that it highlights international heritage collections rarely seen in mainstream venues.

landmarks.name: Leyton Library
landmarks.snippet: Leyton Library is a public lending library and local heritage centre. It matters as a civic hub for education and community events in the borough. Most interesting fact: the Grade II-listed Carnegie library opened in 1907 with an original clock tower still intact.

landmarks.name: Leyton Orient Football Club
landmarks.snippet: Leyton Orient FC is a historic football club founded in 1881, one of the oldest in London. It matters as a community anchor and East London sporting institution. Most interesting fact: the club played at Brisbane Road since 1930 and survived near-liquidation in 2006 through fan ownership.

landmarks.name: Little Flower Parish
landmarks.snippet: Little Flower Parish is a Roman Catholic church serving Regina's faithful with masses and outreach. It stands as an important spiritual center for the community. Established to meet growing Catholic needs, it features traditional architecture tied to the city's immigrant heritage.

landmarks.name: Lord Buddha Temple (four face buddha)
landmarks.snippet: Lord Buddha Temple houses a revered four-faced Buddha statue. It matters as a popular interfaith worship site blending Thai and Chinese traditions. The most interesting fact is devotees circling it clockwise three times for good fortune.

landmarks.name: Lord of Life Lutheran Church
landmarks.snippet: A modern Lutheran church serving the local community. It matters as a center for worship and outreach. The most interesting fact is its welcoming design that fosters inclusive gatherings.

landmarks.name: Lyceum Theatre
landmarks.snippet: The Lyceum Theatre is the oldest continually operating Broadway venue, built in 1903. It is the first theatre to be designated a New York City landmark and still uses its original external electric sign.

landmarks.name: Mémorial des Martyrs de la Déportation
landmarks.snippet: The Mémorial des Martyrs de la Déportation is a memorial on the Île de la Cité honoring French victims deported to Nazi camps. It matters as a solemn reminder of World War II atrocities. Its most interesting fact is its crypt containing ashes from concentration camps.

landmarks.name: Madame Tussauds Las Vegas
landmarks.snippet: A wax museum on the Las Vegas Strip featuring hyper-realistic figures of celebrities, athletes, and historical icons. It opened in 1999 and draws over a million visitors annually. The museum's interactive exhibits include a 4D Marvel experience and a rotating exhibit of pop-culture figures.

landmarks.name: Malý belvedér
landmarks.snippet: Malý belvedér is a scenic viewpoint within Prague Castle offering panoramic city vistas. It matters as a popular spot for visitors seeking classic Prague views. The most interesting fact is it provides one of the best elevated perspectives over the historic Lesser Town rooftops.

landmarks.name: Mandal kirke
landmarks.snippet: Mandal kirke is a historic wooden church in Mandal, Norway, built in 1821 as the town's main place of worship. It matters for its neoclassical design and role in local religious life. The single most interesting fact is its 1800s pipe organ with original mechanics still in use.

landmarks.name: Mandal museum
landmarks.snippet: Mandal museum is a regional museum in Mandal preserving local art, history, and culture. It matters as the primary institution documenting the area's heritage. The single most interesting fact is its collection of works by native artist Amaldus Nielsen displayed in his former home.

landmarks.name: Manly Art Gallery & Museum
landmarks.snippet: Established in 1930, it is Sydney’s oldest suburban art gallery. The most interesting fact is its collection of over 2,000 artworks focused on the Northern Beaches’ maritime and Indigenous heritage.

landmarks.name: Manly Beach
landmarks.snippet: Manly Beach is a world-famous surf beach on Sydney’s Northern Beaches. It has been a major recreational destination since the 1850s and is renowned for its ocean pool and surf lifesaving culture.

landmarks.name: Maritime Museum
landmarks.snippet: The Maritime Museum showcases the area’s seafaring heritage and naval connections. Its prized exhibit is the fully intact 19th-century lighthouse optic that guided ships through Jervis Bay for over a century.

landmarks.name: Masjid Ilyas
landmarks.snippet: Masjid Ilyas is a mosque serving the Muslim population in East Ham. It provides prayer facilities and community programs. The mosque reflects the multicultural character of modern Newham.

landmarks.name: Masjid Sallim Mattar
landmarks.snippet: Masjid Sallim Mattar is a historic mosque in Paya Lebar. It matters as a key place of worship and community gathering for Muslims. The most interesting fact is its establishment in 1956 by the Sallim Mattar family.

landmarks.name: McPhail Memorial Baptist Church
landmarks.snippet: McPhail Memorial Baptist Church is a historic Baptist church in Ottawa's Centretown. It matters for its role in local religious and community life since 1890. The church features distinctive Romanesque Revival architecture with a prominent corner tower.

landmarks.name: Memorial Day Massacre of 1937
landmarks.snippet: Memorial Day Massacre of 1937 is a memorial marking the 1937 steelworkers' strike where Chicago police killed 10 unarmed demonstrators. It matters as a pivotal labor rights tragedy. The most interesting fact is that a Paramount newsreel captured the event, helping expose police brutality nationwide.

landmarks.name: Memorial Wall
landmarks.snippet: Memorial Wall is a public memorial honoring local service members. It matters as a community site of remembrance and reflection. The most interesting fact is its design integrates names of fallen veterans from multiple conflicts.

landmarks.name: Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra
landmarks.snippet: A memorial honoring Spain's greatest writer. It matters as tribute to the author of Don Quixote, foundational to modern literature. The most interesting fact is its location near his final residence in the Barrio de las Letras.

landmarks.name: Miradouro do Pau da Bandeira
landmarks.snippet: Miradouro do Pau da Bandeira is a clifftop viewpoint offering sweeping panoramic views over Albufeira’s old town and Atlantic coastline. It matters as one of the most photographed scenic spots in the region. The single most interesting fact is that its name derives from a long-gone flagpole used for signaling ships.

landmarks.name: Moai
landmarks.snippet: Moai are monumental stone statues created by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island. They represent deified ancestors and embody the island's unique Polynesian culture. Most were carved between 1250 and 1500 CE from volcanic tuff at Rano Raraku quarry.

landmarks.name: Monumento ao Pescador
landmarks.snippet: Monumento ao Pescador is a bronze statue honoring Albufeira’s fishing community and its maritime traditions. It matters as a cultural symbol of the town’s coastal identity. The single most interesting fact is that it was unveiled on the exact spot where fishermen once launched their boats.

landmarks.name: Monumento en honor a los abogados de Atocha
landmarks.snippet: A memorial commemorating lawyers murdered by far-right extremists in 1977. It matters as symbol of Spain's democratic transition after Franco. The most interesting fact is the annual wreath-laying by political leaders on the anniversary.

landmarks.name: Most Holy Trinity Church
landmarks.snippet: Most Holy Trinity Church is a Victorian Roman Catholic church in central Newquay. It matters for serving the town's Catholic community since 1903. Its ornate interior features beautiful stained glass.

landmarks.name: Musée Adam Mickiewicz
landmarks.snippet: Musée Adam Mickiewicz is a museum dedicated to the Polish poet Adam Mickiewicz. It matters as a center for Polish heritage in Paris. Its most interesting fact is it houses the poet's death mask and personal relics from his time in exile.

landmarks.name: Museo archeologico al Teatro Romano
landmarks.snippet: The Museo archeologico al Teatro Romano displays Roman artifacts found at the theatre site. It matters for preserving Verona's ancient history within the historic venue. Its most interesting fact is a 1st-century mosaic floor depicting theatre masks uncovered during 20th-century digs.

landmarks.name: Museo Policía Municipal de Madrid
landmarks.snippet: Housed in a 19th-century police station, it displays uniforms, vehicles and artifacts tracing Madrid’s law enforcement from 1844 onward.

landmarks.name: Museu da Sociedade de Geografia de Lisboa
landmarks.snippet: It is a museum showcasing Portugal's Age of Discoveries with rare maps and artifacts. It preserves the legacy of Portuguese explorers and navigators.

landmarks.name: Museu de Lagos Doutor José Formosinho
landmarks.snippet: Museum preserving Lagos history and artifacts. Matters as the city's main cultural repository. Most interesting fact: houses rare prehistoric and maritime relics from the Age of Discovery.

landmarks.name: Museu Judaico de São Paulo
landmarks.snippet: Brazil's largest Jewish museum opened in 2023 inside the historic 1940s Matarazzo building. Features the oldest Torah scroll in Latin America, dating to 1450.

landmarks.name: Museu Municipal de Arqueologia
landmarks.snippet: Museu Municipal de Arqueologia displays artifacts from local excavations spanning Roman to Moorish periods. It matters as the key institution preserving Albufeira’s archaeological heritage. The single most interesting fact is that it houses a rare Roman mosaic floor unearthed beneath the old town streets.

landmarks.name: Museum of Broadway
landmarks.snippet: The Museum of Broadway chronicles the history of New York theatre from the 1700s to today. It features the largest collection of Broadway artifacts and opened in 2022 inside the special effects shop of the Lyceum Theatre.

landmarks.name: Museum of Illusions Boston
landmarks.snippet: Museum of Illusions Boston displays interactive optical illusions and puzzles. It opened in 2022 inside a historic waterfront building, drawing visitors to experience perception tricks firsthand.

landmarks.name: 大牛稠福德宮
landmarks.snippet: A traditional temple dedicated to the Earth God. It matters as a center of local worship and community rituals. Most interesting fact: hosts an annual temple fair drawing worshippers from across northern Taiwan.

landmarks.name: 八幡宮旧跡
landmarks.snippet: The former site of a historic Hachiman shrine. It matters for marking ancient religious importance. The most interesting fact is its connection to samurai-era dedications.

landmarks.name: 许燎源现代设计艺术博物馆
landmarks.snippet: A private museum showcasing contemporary Chinese design and industrial art. Founded by designer Xu Liaoyuan, it features a unique 1970s factory building with his personal collection.

landmarks.name: 林口聖華壇
landmarks.snippet: A Taoist altar for spiritual practices and ceremonies. It matters for preserving folk religion traditions in the area. Most interesting fact: known for rare spirit-writing sessions held during major festivals.

landmarks.name: 護良親王首洗井戸
landmarks.snippet: A memorial well linked to Prince Moriyoshi. It matters as a site of tragic imperial history. The most interesting fact is the legend of the prince's head being washed here after execution.

landmarks.name: 國家檔案館
landmarks.snippet: A national archive preserving Taiwan's government records and historical documents. It matters as the central repository for the nation's documentary heritage. Most interesting fact: it houses original presidential papers dating back to the early ROC era.

landmarks.name: 新北市圖書館林口分館
landmarks.snippet: A branch library serving readers in Linkou District. It matters as a key cultural and educational hub for residents. Most interesting fact: features extensive local history collections unique to New Taipei.

landmarks.name: 三圣花乡
landmarks.snippet: A renowned flower-themed scenic area in Chengdu, famous for its vast floral fields. It originated from a 2004 rural tourism project that transformed local villages into cultural art zones.

landmarks.name: 东篱菊园
landmarks.snippet: A tranquil chrysanthemum garden with traditional Chinese landscaping. It draws inspiration from ancient poet Tao Yuanming, emphasizing harmony between nature and classical culture.

landmarks.name: National Theatre
landmarks.snippet: The National Theatre is Britain's premier playhouse, opened in 1976 on the South Bank. It has staged landmark productions of classics and new works. Its brutalist design by Denys Lasdun sparked architectural debate.

landmarks.name: 幸福梅林
landmarks.snippet: A plum blossom forest in Chengdu, popular for seasonal flower viewing. It became a local landmark after hosting the 2003 China Plum Blossom Festival.

landmarks.name: 成正寺
landmarks.snippet: A Buddhist temple serving as a place of worship and meditation. It matters for preserving traditional practices and local heritage. The most interesting fact is its role in hosting annual memorial ceremonies for ancestors.

landmarks.name: New Apostolic Church
landmarks.snippet: An active congregation of the New Apostolic faith. It matters as one of Chestermere’s few purpose-built churches. The most interesting fact is its modern design featuring a large central cross visible across the lake.

landmarks.name: Newquay Water Sports Centre
landmarks.snippet: Newquay Water Sports Centre is a modern facility offering surfing and watersports tuition on Fistral Beach. It matters as a hub for Cornwall's surf culture and tourism. The most interesting fact is Fistral Beach hosted the first British professional surfing contest in 1974.

landmarks.name: 王子神社
landmarks.snippet: A Shinto shrine dedicated to the deity of Prince Shotoku. It matters as a local center for worship and community rituals. The most interesting fact is its founding legend ties it to imperial history in the area.

landmarks.name: 瑞穂神社
landmarks.snippet: A Shinto shrine focused on rice harvest and prosperity deities. It matters as a cultural hub for seasonal festivals. The most interesting fact is its annual rice-planting ritual drawing local farmers.

landmarks.name: 林口李科永紀念圖書館
landmarks.snippet: A public library dedicated to local education and reading. It matters for providing community access to knowledge in a growing district. Most interesting fact: named after philanthropist Li Ke-yong who donated land for public learning.

landmarks.name: Old Orchard Street Theatre
landmarks.snippet: Bath’s first purpose-built theatre, opened 1750. Sarah Siddons made her professional debut on this stage, launching one of the greatest acting careers of the Georgian age.

landmarks.name: Old Saint Mary's Church
landmarks.snippet: Chicago's first Roman Catholic cathedral, founded 1833. It is the mother church of the Archdiocese and has witnessed every major chapter of the city's Catholic history.

landmarks.name: Old Spanish Trail City Limit Marker and Bench
landmarks.snippet: Historic roadside marker and bench commemorating the Old Spanish Trail, a major early 20th-century auto route linking the American South and Southwest. It matters as a preserved remnant of early automobile tourism and road development. The single most interesting fact is that it once guided travelers along a 2,500-mile scenic highway from Florida to California.

landmarks.name: One Art Gallery
landmarks.snippet: A contemporary exhibition space showcasing Filipino visual artists, the gallery highlights both established and emerging talents. It frequently hosts talks and workshops that connect local creators with the international art scene.

landmarks.name: Orrido del Bogn
landmarks.snippet: A dramatic gorge carved by the River Bogn near Verzasca. It matters as a striking natural landmark and scenic hiking destination. The most interesting fact is that wooden walkways built in the 19th century still cling to its sheer rock walls.

landmarks.name: Ottawa Chinatown Arch
landmarks.snippet: The Ottawa Chinatown Arch is the ceremonial gateway marking the entrance to Ottawa's Chinatown district. It matters as a cultural symbol of the city's Chinese community. The arch was gifted by Ottawa's sister city Beijing in 2010.

landmarks.name: Our Lady and St Vincent
landmarks.snippet: A Roman Catholic parish church serving the community since 1962. It replaced an earlier tin chapel and remains a spiritual hub for local Catholics.

landmarks.name: Our Lady of Good Voyage Chapel
landmarks.snippet: A small Catholic chapel built in 1952 for Boston's seafarers. It matters as a spiritual haven for the working waterfront community. The most interesting fact is its name honors Portuguese fishermen who donated the original bell.

landmarks.name: Our Lady Of Nazareth Catholic Church
landmarks.snippet: Our Lady Of Nazareth Catholic Church is a Catholic parish established for Italian and Mexican immigrants. It matters as a spiritual and social hub on the East Side. The most interesting fact is its annual Feast of Our Lady draws thousands for processions and Italian-Mexican fusion cuisine.

landmarks.name: Our Lady of the Alps
landmarks.snippet: Our Lady of the Alps is a historic Catholic church in Franz Josef, serving the spiritual needs of the local and tourist community. It matters as a cultural anchor in a remote alpine setting. The church features a distinctive alpine architectural style reflecting early European settler influence.

landmarks.name: Our Savior Lutheran Church
landmarks.snippet: Our Savior Lutheran Church serves as a historic place of worship in Watertown. It matters for its longstanding role in community religious life since its founding.

landmarks.name: Parroquia de San Nicolás
landmarks.snippet: A historic church in Madrid's literary quarter. It matters as one of the city's oldest parishes with medieval origins. The single most interesting fact is its 12th-century tower, the oldest surviving structure in Madrid.

landmarks.name: Parroquia Santo Cristo del Olivar
landmarks.snippet: Parroquia Santo Cristo del Olivar is a historic church in central Madrid serving as a neighborhood spiritual hub. It matters for its Baroque architecture and community role. The most interesting fact is its name honors an olive tree legend tied to local miracles in the 17th century.

landmarks.name: Pelourinho de Lagos
landmarks.snippet: Historic stone pillory marking the old town square. Matters as a symbol of municipal authority. Most interesting fact: dates to the 15th century and witnessed public punishments.

landmarks.name: Piemineklis Mihailam Tālam
landmarks.snippet: Monument to chess world champion Mikhail Tal. It honors the Riga-born grandmaster known for his brilliant and aggressive style.

landmarks.name: Podtatranské múzeum
landmarks.snippet: The regional museum showcases Spiš history and Tatra culture. Its most notable exhibit is a preserved 19th-century wooden house interior from the High Tatras.

landmarks.name: Ponte Pietra
landmarks.snippet: Ponte Pietra is Verona's oldest surviving Roman bridge, dating to the 1st century BC. It matters as a vital link across the Adige that has withstood floods and wars. Its most interesting fact is that after WWII bombing, locals retrieved and rebuilt the original Roman stones.

landmarks.name: Potters Bar Memorial Gardens
landmarks.snippet: A tranquil memorial park dedicated to local war veterans. The gardens were created after World War II to honor Potters Bar residents who served and died in both world wars.

landmarks.name: Potters Bar War Memorial
landmarks.snippet: A striking stone memorial commemorating local fallen soldiers. It stands as the town’s central tribute and is the focus of Remembrance Sunday services each year.

landmarks.name: Pražský hrad
landmarks.snippet: Pražský hrad is the largest ancient castle complex in the world and seat of Czech power for over a millennium. It matters as the historic center of Bohemia and the Czech Republic. The most interesting fact is it houses the Bohemian Crown Jewels kept in St. Vitus Cathedral.

landmarks.name: Presidio of Monterey Museum
landmarks.snippet: A museum on the historic Presidio of Monterey military post. It preserves Monterey's Spanish, Mexican and American military history. The Presidio was founded in 1770 as one of California's first European settlements.

landmarks.name: Prince of Wales Branch
landmarks.snippet: Prince of Wales Branch is a neighborhood library in Regina offering reading materials and community events. It plays a key role in promoting literacy and cultural access. Opened as part of the city's library expansion, it supports lifelong learning for residents.

landmarks.name: Quaibrücke
landmarks.snippet: Quaibrücke is a historic bridge connecting central Zurich districts across the Limmat River. It matters as a key transport and scenic link. The most interesting fact is its reconstruction in 1884 following earlier wooden structures dating to the 12th century.

landmarks.name: Queenscliff Beach
landmarks.snippet: Queenscliff Beach is a scenic attraction north of Manly, popular for swimming and its quieter vibe compared to the main beach. It matters as part of Sydney's iconic coastline. The most interesting fact is its proximity to the historic Queenscliff Bathers Pavilion.

landmarks.name: Quincy Market
landmarks.snippet: Quincy Market is a 1825 granite market hall built to expand Boston's food trade. Its most striking feature is the 535-foot-long colonnaded building topped by a copper dome.

landmarks.name: Rīgas cirks
landmarks.snippet: Riga Circus is one of Europe's oldest permanent circuses, established in 1888. It matters as a beloved cultural institution blending entertainment and tradition. Most interesting fact: the historic wooden arena building remains largely unchanged since its opening.

landmarks.name: Ramakrishna Mission
landmarks.snippet: Ramakrishna Mission is a spiritual and educational center. It matters for promoting Vedanta philosophy and social service in Singapore. The most interesting fact is its founding in 1928 as one of the oldest Hindu missions here.

landmarks.name: Real Fábrica de Tapices
landmarks.snippet: A royal tapestry factory founded in 1720 by Philip V. It supplied the Spanish court and still produces handwoven pieces using 18th-century looms.

landmarks.name: Real Teatro de Retiro
landmarks.snippet: A 17th-century court theatre once used by Spanish monarchs. It hosted early zarzuela performances and remains a symbol of Madrid’s theatrical heritage.

landmarks.name: Riviera Theatre
landmarks.snippet: Riviera Theatre is a historic live music venue in Chicago. It matters for hosting legendary performers since the 1980s. The most interesting fact is that it was originally a movie theater built in 1918 and converted to a concert hall in 1986.

landmarks.name: S. Maria Assunta
landmarks.snippet: The main parish church of Mergoscia, dating to the 14th century. It matters as the spiritual heart of the lakeside village. The most interesting fact is that its Baroque high altar contains a 16th-century wooden crucifix believed to have miraculously survived a fire.

landmarks.name: Sailors Grave
landmarks.snippet: Sailors Grave is a coastal memorial marking the burial site of two sailors lost in the 1870 wreck of the schooner Rover. Local Indigenous oral history recounts the rescue of a lone survivor by local clanspeople.

landmarks.name: Saint Ambrose Catholic Church
landmarks.snippet: A Roman Catholic parish in Annandale, VA, founded in 1964 amid suburban growth. It serves a diverse community and emphasizes social outreach. Fact: Named after St. Ambrose of Milan, a Doctor of the Church, it hosted notable visits by bishops during Vatican II era.

landmarks.name: Saint James Church
landmarks.snippet: Saint James Church is an Anglican church in the heart of Franz Josef, notable for its role in community gatherings and services. It matters as a preserved example of early 20th-century ecclesiastical architecture. The church was built in 1931 and survived multiple glacial floods.

landmarks.name: Saint John's, Waterloo
landmarks.snippet: Saint John's, Waterloo is a Georgian church built in 1824 as a Waterloo victory memorial. It was rebuilt after 1940 bombing. The adjacent garden features a memorial to the 1944 Warsaw Uprising.

landmarks.name: Saint John the Baptist Catholic Church
landmarks.snippet: Saint John the Baptist Catholic Church is a historic Catholic parish serving Polish and Latino communities. It matters for its role in immigrant integration since 1903. The most interesting fact is its annual Dozynki harvest festival features Polish folk dances and pierogi sales.

landmarks.name: Saint Mary's Church
landmarks.snippet: Saint Mary's Church is the historic parish church in Princes Risborough. It matters as a Grade I listed building central to local religious and community life for centuries. The most interesting fact is its 13th-century chancel arch and medieval wall paintings.

landmarks.name: Saint Michael the Archangel Catholic Church
landmarks.snippet: Saint Michael the Archangel Catholic Church serves Silver Spring's Catholic community. It matters as a spiritual and social anchor for local families since the mid-20th century. The single most interesting fact is its 1954 cornerstone was laid by Cardinal Spellman.

landmarks.name: Saint Paul's Episcopal Church
landmarks.snippet: Utah's oldest continuously used Episcopal church, consecrated in 1881. It symbolizes the arrival of non-Mormon religious communities during the mining boom and serves as a downtown architectural landmark.

landmarks.name: Saint Stanislaus Roman Catholic Church
landmarks.snippet: A historic Roman Catholic church serving Polish-American parishioners. It matters as a cornerstone of ethnic heritage and faith in the area. The most interesting fact is its founding by Polish immigrants in the late 19th century, featuring traditional architecture.

landmarks.name: Saint Vincent de Paul Catholic Church
landmarks.snippet: Saint Vincent de Paul Catholic Church is a historic church in San Diego serving the local community. It matters for its charitable outreach and architectural significance. The single most interesting historical fact is that it was established to support immigrants in the early 20th century.

landmarks.name: Salt Lake Masonic Temple
landmarks.snippet: Built in 1927 as a grand Masonic lodge, its Egyptian Revival façade and lavish interior halls make it one of Utah's most distinctive non-religious landmarks and a venue for private cultural events.

landmarks.name: Sankt Theresia
landmarks.snippet: Sankt Theresia is a Catholic parish church in Munich serving the local community since its consecration. It matters as a spiritual and architectural anchor in the neighborhood. The single most interesting fact is that its modern design incorporates post-war reconstruction elements reflecting Munich's recovery.

landmarks.name: Sawtell Chilli Festival
landmarks.snippet: The Sawtell Chilli Festival is an annual food-and-music event. It matters as a celebration of local produce and culture. The most interesting fact is the chilli-eating contest crowns a new champion each year.

landmarks.name: Sawtell Headland
landmarks.snippet: Sawtell Headland is a coastal viewpoint offering panoramic ocean vistas. It matters for whale watching and sunsets. The most interesting fact is Indigenous middens nearby reveal continuous occupation for over 6,000 years.

landmarks.name: Second Presbyterian Church
landmarks.snippet: Built 1874 in Gothic Revival style, this National Historic Landmark contains the largest intact collection of Louis Comfort Tiffany stained-glass windows in the world.

landmarks.name: Serbian Saint Simeon Mirotociv Orthodox Church
landmarks.snippet: Serbian Saint Simeon Mirotociv Orthodox Church is an Eastern Orthodox church founded by Serbian immigrants. It matters as a cultural anchor for Chicago's Serbian diaspora. The most interesting fact is its annual Slava feast honors Saint Simeon with traditional Serbian music and foods.

landmarks.name: Simon Bamberger House
landmarks.snippet: Home of Utah's first Jewish governor and the state's fourth. Built in 1898, this Queen Anne residence reflects the rise of immigrant entrepreneurs who helped shape Utah's political and cultural landscape.

landmarks.name: Sligo Church
landmarks.snippet: Sligo Church is a prominent Seventh-day Adventist congregation in Takoma Park. It matters for its large, diverse community and historic role in Adventist education. The single most interesting fact is its founding in 1907 helped establish the area as an Adventist center.

landmarks.name: Southbank Centre
landmarks.snippet: Southbank Centre is the UK's largest arts complex, opened in 1951 for the Festival of Britain. It hosts concerts, exhibitions and theatre. The Royal Festival Hall remains its iconic concert venue.

landmarks.name: Sparks Street Lookout
landmarks.snippet: Sparks Street Lookout is a public viewpoint overlooking the Sparks Street Mall and surrounding downtown. It matters as a popular spot for visitors to enjoy city views. The mall below was Canada's first pedestrian-only street, opened in 1967.

landmarks.name: St Andrew's Church, Hatfield Peverel
landmarks.snippet: St Andrew's Church is a historic parish church in Hatfield Peverel, Essex. It matters as a key religious and architectural landmark dating back to the 12th century. The most interesting fact is that it incorporates remains of a former Benedictine priory dissolved in 1536.

landmarks.name: St Dunstan's
landmarks.snippet: St Dunstan's is a historic church in the Princes Risborough area. It matters as an active place of worship with centuries of local significance. The most interesting fact is its dedication to St Dunstan, a key figure in Anglo-Saxon religious reform.

landmarks.name: 聖約翰座堂 St. John's Cathedral
landmarks.snippet: St. John's Cathedral is the oldest surviving Western ecclesiastical building in Hong Kong. It matters as the mother church of the Anglican Diocese. The most interesting fact is its bell tower served as a Japanese lookout post during the 1941 occupation.

landmarks.name: St Mark Coptic Orthodox Church
landmarks.snippet: Historic Coptic church serving Monterey's Egyptian Christian community. It represents cultural diversity in a city known for its Spanish and American roots.

landmarks.name: St. Mary's Catholic Church
landmarks.snippet: Constructed in 1858, St Mary’s is the oldest Catholic church on Sydney’s Northern Beaches. Its most interesting fact is the rare 1860 stained-glass windows imported from Birmingham.

landmarks.name: St Mary's
landmarks.snippet: The historic parish church of Potters Bar, dating back to the 13th century. Its tower once guided travelers on the Great North Road.

landmarks.name: St. Matthews Anglican Church
landmarks.snippet: Built in 1864, St Matthew’s is one of Manly’s oldest surviving churches. Its most interesting feature is the original 1865 pipe organ, still played for services today.

landmarks.name: St Michael the Archangel
landmarks.snippet: St Michael the Archangel is Newquay's main parish church built in 1910. It matters as the spiritual centre for the growing seaside town. Its striking granite tower dominates the skyline.

landmarks.name: St Patrick's Cemetery chapel
landmarks.snippet: St Patrick’s Cemetery chapel is a small Gothic Revival chapel within the historic Roman Catholic burial ground. It matters as a quiet heritage site linked to 19th-century Irish immigration. Most interesting fact: it contains the grave of the last-known survivor of the Battle of Trafalgar.

landmarks.name: St Patrick's Seminary
landmarks.snippet: Completed in 1889, this imposing Gothic Revival building once trained Catholic priests. Its most interesting feature is the 40-metre bell tower that dominates the Manly skyline.

landmarks.name: St. Peter
landmarks.snippet: St. Peter is Zurich's oldest parish church with the largest clock face in Europe. It matters as a central religious and architectural landmark since the 13th century. The single most interesting fact is its 1534 tower clock with a 9-meter diameter face.

landmarks.name: St. Sava Serbian Eastern Orthodox Church
landmarks.snippet: St. Sava Serbian Eastern Orthodox Church is a place of worship. It matters for preserving Serbian Orthodox heritage locally. The most interesting fact is its veneration of St. Sava, founder of the Serbian Orthodox Church.

landmarks.name: Starý královský palác
landmarks.snippet: Starý královský palác served as the main residence of Bohemian kings inside Prague Castle. It matters as the historic seat of royal power. The most interesting fact is the 1618 Defenestration of Prague occurred from its windows, sparking the Thirty Years' War.

landmarks.name: 皇后像廣場 Statue Square
landmarks.snippet: Statue Square is a central public plaza in Hong Kong's Central district. It matters as the historic heart of the city's financial and civic life. The most interesting fact is that its statues of British figures were removed during WWII and later replaced with a modern fountain.

landmarks.name: Submarine
landmarks.snippet: Memorial submarine display highlighting naval heritage. It commemorates Monterey's role in Pacific submarine operations during World War II.

landmarks.name: Suncoast Cathedral
landmarks.snippet: Suncoast Cathedral is a place of worship. It matters as a prominent religious landmark serving the community. The most interesting fact is its role in hosting large-scale worship services and events.

landmarks.name: Svētā Jāņa baznīca
landmarks.snippet: St. John's Church is a historic Lutheran church in Riga's Old Town, dating back to the 13th century. It matters as one of Riga's oldest surviving religious sites. Most interesting fact: its distinctive stepped gable facade was added during 15th-century Gothic reconstruction.

landmarks.name: Swedish American Museum
landmarks.snippet: Swedish American Museum is a cultural institution preserving Swedish heritage in Chicago. It matters as the only museum in the US dedicated to Swedish-American history. The most interesting fact is that it was founded in 1976 by a group of Swedish immigrants in Andersonville.

landmarks.name: Tadeusz Kościuszko
landmarks.snippet: A memorial statue honoring Tadeusz Kościuszko, the Polish military leader who aided American independence. It matters as a tribute to his Revolutionary War contributions. The most interesting fact is that Kościuszko also designed key fortifications at West Point.

landmarks.name: Teatro Azares
landmarks.snippet: Teatro Azares is a contemporary independent theatre venue in Santiago known for experimental and fringe productions. It supports emerging Chilean playwrights and performers. Its notable feature is hosting the annual Festival de Dramaturgia Nacional since the early 2000s.

landmarks.name: Teatro Brasileiro de Comédia
landmarks.snippet: Pioneering Brazilian theater founded in 1948, birthplace of modern Brazilian stage. The 1950s building hosted the first professional theater company in the country.

landmarks.name: Teatro Monumental
landmarks.snippet: A major concert hall and theater known for classical music performances. It matters as a key cultural venue hosting the RTVE Symphony Orchestra. The most interesting fact is its 1920s Art Deco interior hidden behind a neoclassical facade.

landmarks.name: Teatro Nacional Dona Maria II
landmarks.snippet: It is Lisbon's premier national theatre and a symbol of Portuguese cultural identity. It opened in 1846 and was named after Queen Maria II.

landmarks.name: Teatro Nuevo Apolo
landmarks.snippet: Teatro Nuevo Apolo is a historic theatre in Madrid's Lavapiés district known for its role in Spanish performing arts. It matters as a key venue for contemporary and classic productions. The most interesting fact is that it was rebuilt in 1984 after a fire, reviving a 19th-century theatre tradition.

landmarks.name: Teatro Romano
landmarks.snippet: The Teatro Romano is a well-preserved 1st-century BC Roman theatre built into a hillside. It matters as one of Italy's earliest stone theatres still hosting performances. Its most interesting fact is that excavations in the 19th century uncovered a Roman villa beneath the stage area.

landmarks.name: The Brook
landmarks.snippet: The Brook is a place of worship in Stratford known for its community focus. It has long served as a spiritual hub for local residents. The site reflects the area's diverse religious heritage.

landmarks.name: 和平紀念碑 The Cenotaph
landmarks.snippet: The Cenotaph is a war memorial in Statue Square honoring those who died in the World Wars. It matters as Hong Kong's main site for Remembrance Day ceremonies. The most interesting fact is it was modeled after the Cenotaph in London's Whitehall.

landmarks.name: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
landmarks.snippet: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is a place of worship. It matters as a center for local members of this global faith community. The most interesting fact is that its teachings emphasize family history and genealogy research.

landmarks.name: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
landmarks.snippet: Worldwide Christian denomination founded by Joseph Smith in 1830 in New York. Matters for its 17 million members and global humanitarian reach. Its Salt Lake Temple took 40 years to build and is the church's most sacred structure.

landmarks.name: The Institute of Contemporary Art
landmarks.snippet: Boston's premier contemporary art museum on the waterfront since 1936. It matters for showcasing cutting-edge art in a dramatic harbor setting. The most interesting fact is its building is a renovated 1930s police and fire boat headquarters.

landmarks.name: The Louisville Palace Theater
landmarks.snippet: The Louisville Palace Theater is a historic 1928 movie palace renowned for its opulent Spanish Baroque interior with intricate murals and chandelier. It matters as a premier live performance venue; Louis Armstrong premiered his song 'Louisiana' here in 1930.

landmarks.name: The Old Vic
landmarks.snippet: The Old Vic is a historic theatre founded in 1818, renowned for its Shakespeare productions and as the former home of the National Theatre company. It was rebuilt after wartime bombing and hosted stars like Laurence Olivier.

landmarks.name: The Pines
landmarks.snippet: A poignant memorial in Bailey's Crossroads, VA, commemorating Vietnamese refugees who died fleeing communism. It symbolizes resilience. Fact: Dedicated in 2003, it honors the 'boat people' tragedy, with over 200 names etched on its walls.

landmarks.name: The Pump Room
landmarks.snippet: Elegant 1790s salon where Georgian society gathered to drink mineral water. Jane Austen set scenes here; its chandeliers and string trio still evoke that era of polite society.

landmarks.name: The Ravine
landmarks.snippet: An intimate theater space known for experimental and student productions. It matters as an alternative arts venue fostering local creativity. The most interesting fact is its location in a converted natural ravine adding unique acoustics and atmosphere.

landmarks.name: The Roman Baths
landmarks.snippet: Britain's best-preserved Roman spa complex, built around AD 70 and central to the cult of Sulis Minerva. The most striking fact is that the sacred spring still flows at 46°C, exactly as it did two millennia ago.

landmarks.name: The Silver Pass
landmarks.snippet: The Silver Pass is a public artwork in Silver Spring celebrating local transit history. It matters as a landmark sculpture marking the area's Metrorail connection. The single most interesting fact is its design incorporates actual rail spikes from the old B&O line.

landmarks.name: The Spirit of Monterey Wax Museum
landmarks.snippet: Wax museum showcasing Monterey's history through lifelike figures. It brings to life key moments from the city's Spanish, Mexican, and American eras.

landmarks.name: The Studio Door
landmarks.snippet: The Studio Door is an art gallery in San Diego promoting contemporary local artists. It matters as a hub for creative expression and community engagement. The single most interesting historical fact is that it has hosted exhibitions featuring emerging talents since its founding.

landmarks.name: Theater PATHOS München
landmarks.snippet: Theater PATHOS München is an independent theatre venue hosting contemporary performances and events. It matters as a cultural hub for experimental arts in the city. The single most interesting fact is its origins in a former industrial space repurposed for creative expression.

landmarks.name: Thermae Bath Spa
